# `silk/git/refs`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Git object ids, references, and the lists of references that a remote or a local repository
has.

## When to use
Use the types here with `silk.git.remote`, which lists the references of a remote repository
like `git ls-remote`, and `silk.git.local`, which reads them from a `.git` directory. Look a
name up in a [`RefList`](#RefList) with [`RefList.find`](#RefList.impl.find) for an exact name such as `refs/tags/v1.0.0`, or
with [`RefList.resolve`](#RefList.impl.resolve) for a short name such as `main` or `v1.0.0`, as Git does.

## Details
An [`ObjectId`](#ObjectId) is a SHA-1 (20 bytes) or SHA-256 (32 bytes) object name. A [`Ref`](#Ref) has a full
name, the object it points at, the object that an annotated tag peels to, and the target of a
symbolic reference such as `HEAD`. [`Ref.commit`](#Ref.impl.commit) gives the peeled object when there is one,
which for a tag is the commit that it tags.

## Errors
- [`GitRefError`](#GitRefError) for the failures of the Git modules, such as a malformed advertisement.
- `OutOfMemoryError` from functions that copy names.

## Examples
### Resolve a short name
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.git.refs { ObjectId, Ref, RefList }

effect fn build() -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let id = match ObjectId.parseHex(b"95d09f2b10159347eece71399a7e2e907ea3df4f") {
    Option<ObjectId>.Some { value } => value
    Option<ObjectId>.None => { return false }
  }
  let mut refs = RefList.make()
  run refs.add(run Ref.make("refs/heads/main", Option<ObjectId>.some(id)))
  return match refs.resolve("main") {
    Option<&Ref>.Some { value } => value.isBranch()
    Option<&Ref>.None => false
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  if run build() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator) {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}
```

Import as `RefList` with `import silk.git.refs { RefList }`.

## `ObjectId`

```silk
pub struct ObjectId
```

The name of a Git object: a SHA-1 of 20 bytes or a SHA-256 of 32 bytes.

### Details

Make one with [`ObjectId.parseHex`](#ObjectId.impl.parseHex) from 40 or 64 hexadecimal digits, or with
[`ObjectId.fromBytes`](#ObjectId.impl.fromBytes). It is a plain value, so copies are cheap. Two ids are equal when
[`ObjectId.equals`](#ObjectId.impl.equals) says so: the same length and the same bytes.

<a id="Ref"></a>

## `Ref`

```silk
pub struct Ref
```

One Git reference: a name, the object it points at, and, for some, a symbolic target or a
peeled object.

### Details

`name` is the full name, such as `HEAD`, `refs/heads/main`, or `refs/tags/v1.0.0`. `id` is the
object that the reference points at. It is `None` only for a symbolic reference whose target
does not exist yet, such as `HEAD` in a new repository. `peeled` is the object that an annotated
tag points at, after all tags are followed, when the source reported it. `target` is the name
that a symbolic reference points at, such as `refs/heads/main` for `HEAD`.

<a id="Ref.name"></a>

<a id="RefList"></a>

## `RefList`

```silk
pub struct RefList
```

The references of one repository, in the order of the source.

### Details

A remote lists its references sorted by name, after `HEAD`. A local repository is read in the
same order. Use [`RefList.find`](#RefList.impl.find) for an exact name, [`RefList.resolve`](#RefList.impl.resolve) for a short name, and
[`RefList.asSlice`](#RefList.impl.asSlice) to walk all of them.

Adds `entry` at the end of the list.

#### Errors

<a id="RefList.impl.insertSorted"></a>

### Method `insertSorted`

```silk
pub effect fn insertSorted(self: &mut Self, entry: Ref) -> usize
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Puts `entry` at its place in name order and returns its index. A reference with the same
name is replaced.

#### Details

Names compare by their bytes, as Git sorts them, so `HEAD` comes before `refs/`. It finds the
place by binary search, so the list must already be in name order, as it is when you only add
references with this function. An entry that sorts last is appended without moving others.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow the list. The list does not change.

#### Gotchas

<a id="RefList.impl.find"></a>

### Method `find`

```silk
pub fn find<'r>(self: &'r Self, name: string) -> Option<&'r Ref>
```

Returns the reference whose full name is exactly `name`, such as `refs/heads/main` or `HEAD`,
or `None` if there is none.

<a id="RefList.impl.resolve"></a>

### Method `resolve`

```silk
pub fn resolve<'r>(self: &'r Self, name: string) -> Option<&'r Ref>
```

Returns the reference that the short name `name` means, in the order that Git uses, or
`None` if there is none.

#### Details

It tries, in order: `name` itself, `refs/<name>`, `refs/tags/<name>`, `refs/heads/<name>`,
`refs/remotes/<name>`, and `refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD`. So a tag wins over a branch with the
same short name, as in `git rev-parse`.

<a id="RefList.impl.head"></a>

### Method `head`

```silk
pub fn head<'r>(self: &'r Self) -> Option<&'r Ref>
```

Returns `HEAD`, or `None` if the source did not report it.

#### Details

For a remote, `HEAD` is the default branch: its `target` is the branch name, such as
`refs/heads/main`, when the server reports it. A detached `HEAD` has no target.

### `Malformed`

```silk

```

The data at `offset` is not in the expected format: a broken pkt-line, a line without an
object id, or a broken `packed-refs` or loose reference file.

```silk
pub offset: usize
```

The byte offset in the response or file where the problem is.
